youtube.title: JAMES CORBETT
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan is joined by investigative journalist James Corbett, founder of The Corbett Report, to revisit the unresolved questions surrounding the September 11th attacks in 2001, now 25 years on. Moving beyond the physics of that day, Corbett traces the financial links behind the alleged hijackers, the CIA's ties to Al-Qaeda and the neoconservative planning that followed. Discover more from James at the Corbett Report For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: ROB MACCULLOCH
youtube.summary: Economist Rob MacCulloch joins Paul Brennan to dissect The Opportunities Party's tax reset policy, arguing its 1.75% land tax stacks on top of existing taxes rather than replacing them, amounting to a major wealth redistribution rather than genuine reform. He also questions National's “no new taxes” pledge given looming fiscal pressures, welcomes compulsory KiwiSaver increases as a rare bright spot, and weighs in on NZ First's push for a state-owned bank amid what he calls rampant profiteering by banks and supermarkets. For more on Rob MacCulloch For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: DON BRASH & MATT ROBSON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan hosts former Reserve Bank governor Don Brash and Auckland barrister and former minister Matt Robson for a wide-ranging political discussion. The pair find surprising common ground on supermarket break-up plans and vague “price gouging” laws, before diverging on Kiwibank's public ownership, tax cuts, and debt reduction. They close with Robson's documentary on the late Jim Anderton and its rocky path to funding. Check out RCR's Wednesday's Webinar: Politics: Has MMP Come of Age, Strategic Voting, Polls and more For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: KIT KNIGHTLY
youtube.summary: OffGuardian editor Kit Knightly joins Paul Brennan to pick apart the vague, escalating warnings around AI extinction risk, from Jacob Coxon's resignation to the Hugging Face “rogue agent” incident. He argues the real danger is the sweeping regulation likely to follow rather than the technology itself. They also mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11, questioning the physical evidence behind the official narrative and the media's recent rehabilitation of George W. Bush. Discover more from Kit at OffGuardian For news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: KATRINA BIGGS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with women's rights advocate Katrina Biggs about the year-long battle to raise New Zealand's first official women's suffrage flag on Parliament's forecourt ahead of Suffrage Day. Katrina recounts the bureaucratic pushback, the legal fight that finally won approval, and the muted turnout from some MPs. The conversation also touches on Parliament's record female representation and the ongoing debate over legal definitions of sex. Discover more from Katrina on Substack For news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.summary: Former Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash joins Maree Buscke for a wide-ranging webinar on strategic voting under MMP, explaining why National's electorate strength could waste its party vote and urging centre-right voters to split their ballots. They cover ballooning government debt, the case for raising the super age, Treaty of Waitangi politics, GST's regressive edge, and why bold fiscal reform has been politically unpalatable since Ruth Richardson. youtube.title: IVOR CUMMINS
youtube.summary: Ivor Cummins joins Paul Brennan from Dublin to recount his close encounter with Trump during the president's recent Irish visit, before turning to demographic data suggesting native Irish could become a minority within decades. They also dissect the backlash over a controversial male lactation conference and debate whether under-16 social media age verification is really about protecting children or ending online anonymity. Discover more from Ivor on his website The Fat Emperor or find him on Facebook and X For news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: LAURA MCCLURE
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with ACT Party List MP Laura McClure about ACT’s new six-point small-business package, including a proposed youth training wage, freezing the minimum wage for three years, union fees and employment rules. They also discuss tax treatment for new technology, immigration settings, supermarket competition, the cost of essentials and ACT’s newly announced list, including Paul Henry’s entry into politics. For more on Laura McClure or find her on Facebook For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: MEDIA MATTERS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Marty Gibson debate the media storm around AI existential risk, sparked by a young ex-Anthropic employee's public warnings and contrasting political reactions from Trump and Christopher Luxon. Maree argues fear over AI safety is being manufactured to entrench a handful of tech giants through capturing regulation, while Marty counters that the danger is real and society lacks the structures to debate it honestly, closing on his case for smaller, human-scale communities as a buffer against technocratic control. For more information check out Reclaim the Net | How the AI safety push creates new gatekeepers For news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.
